components.name: Camera view selector
components.description: Four scene views: Track chaser, ISS + chaser (default), Full ISS, and Target port. Native pressed states identify selection; drag orbits the spacecraft and grid together, and a camera selection resumes automatic placement. Overview and Full ISS fit physical bounds using a bounding sphere, the limiting horizontal or vertical half field of view, and 1.25 padding; resize and NASA ISS loading refit the selected mode. Chaser tracking frames both ports below 10m or after capture.

components.name: Scene overlays and coordinate grid
components.description: Native controls for measured trail, velocity arrow, capture envelopes, and the shared fixed local XYZ grid. Auto spacing uses 10cm below 1m, 1m below 10m, 10m through 200m, and 100m above 200m; five fixed spacings cover 1cm to 100m. The three translucent planes meet at the primary PMA-2 port origin, with X warm red, Y mint, and Z blue plus axis letters. The output states current division size. NASA ISS loading status occupies its own line; asset failure retains the labelled schematic target.

narrative.overview:
The research flight-operations dashboard keeps its graphite, mint, and blue identity. Larger typography, a NASA ISS primary, and a concept chaser give the relative flight scene more presence. Configuration, capture, and guidance stay readable beside the scene so researchers can compare commands with measured effects. The shared XYZ grid makes the same local port coordinates visible from centimetres to hundreds of metres per division.

Motion follows backend measurements and continues while provider guidance is pending. Planning status and decision snapshot provenance remain readable beside current telemetry. A separate, labelled illustrative Earth and static star field frame the spacecraft. Controls remain stable, native, and task-focused; the only authored confirmation animation follows a server-verified capture.
keyCharacteristics: Shared XYZ coordinates at true metre scale
Measured motion with a labelled illustrative backdrop
Visible guidance state and decision snapshot provenance
dos: Do show units beside every configurable quantity and measurement.
Do keep numerical telemetry tied to backend events.
Do label the deterministic planner and provider fallback honestly.
Do keep planning activity, current telemetry, and request-time reasoning separately labelled.
Do expose decision snapshot age and whether a returned proposal was applied or discarded.
Do preserve standard form semantics and reduced-motion behavior.
Do identify the NASA ISS, concept chaser, fallback target, and illustrative scenery explicitly.
Do share the local coordinate frame and true metre scale across models, grid, and telemetry.
Do keep grid spacing and visibility in native labelled controls, with the current division size visible.
Do fit full-scene cameras from physical bounds and the limiting field of view when the canvas resizes.
Do reserve capture confirmation for the server's terminal docked event.
donts: Don't use animation to conceal latency or invent a physical outcome.
Don't turn an observed success rate into an unqualified accuracy guarantee.
